meta.audience: Board of Halvard Freight: the CEO and CFO decide; two non-executive directors will push back on service risk; low technical depth
meta.objective: Approve the consolidation of three depots and release a $2.6M transition budget

meta.title: Six depots do the work of nine

slides.headline: Six depots do the work of nine.
slides.subtitle: Three of them have run below 40% utilisation for six quarters, and Oakmont's lease renews in March at a 12% step-up.
slides.meta: Built on the FY25 depot P&L, the route model v3 and operator interviews from Aug 2026. All figures fictional.
slides.notes: Open on the answer. The provenance line is what buys the room's attention.

slides.headline: Consolidating three depots saves $4.1M a year for a one-time cost of $2.6M, with next-day coverage held for 99.2% of customers.
slides.answer: Consolidating three depots saves $4.1M a year for a one-time cost of $2.6M, with next-day coverage held for 99.2% of customers.

slides.notes: The whole deck on one slide. A reader may stop here; nothing below should surprise them.

slides.headline: Three depots have run below 45% utilisation for six quarters.
slides.subtitle: Dock hours used over dock hours available, by quarter.
slides.notes: Let the pattern land: six quarters, not a blip. The three rows at the bottom are the case.
slides.band: Three depots carry $5.2M of fixed cost for 14% of network volume.

slides.headline: Three separate changes emptied the same three depots.
slides.subtitle: None of the three was a mistake; together they left the network one size too big.
slides.notes: Pre-empts 'whose fault': nobody's. The Carver loss is public knowledge on the board.

causes.title: Easton expansion (2023)
causes.body: Added dock capacity 41 miles from Brookline.

causes.title: Parcel mix shift
causes.body: Smaller consignments consolidate better at larger sites.

slides.effectBody: $5.2M of lease and labour carrying 14% of network volume.

slides.headline: Easton and Fairmont score highest on every criterion but one.
slides.subtitle: Scored by the route model and site visits; full = strongest on that criterion.
slides.notes: Access is Easton's weak criterion: the yard entrance. Say it before the NED asks.
slides.band: Their volume fits inside Easton and Fairmont with 18% headroom, and next-day coverage holds for 99.2% of customers.
slides.legend: Full = strongest on that criterion; empty = weakest.

slides.headline: Of 2,140 customers, 17 would lose next-day service.
slides.subtitle: Route model v3, current order book, receiving sites' drive-time windows.
slides.notes: The 17 are rural. Name them in backup; offer the later cut-off to the 62.

stages.title: Customers served by the three depots
stages.note: All accounts routed through Ridgeway, Brookline or Oakmont.

stages.title: Re-routable within the model
stages.note: Fit within receiving sites' drive-time windows.

stages.title: Lose next-day service
stages.note: Rural addresses beyond the two-hour window.

slides.headline: Gross saving of $4.4M nets to $4.1M after fuel.
slides.subtitle: Annual run-rate after transition, $M.
slides.notes: Fuel is the only cost that rises. It is included, not hidden.
slides.band: The saving is $4.1M a year net, for a one-time cost of $2.6M, with payback inside eight months.

card.kicker: What is not in the bridge
card.title: One-time costs

slides.headline: Savings start in month four and reach run-rate in month ten.
slides.subtitle: Routes move before people; people move before buildings close.
slides.notes: The sequence is the risk control: nothing closes until the pilot holds service.

slides.headline: 3 risks, each with an owner and a mitigation.

rows.risk: Union consultation at Ridgeway extends beyond four months
rows.mitigation: Start informal engagement now; sequence Oakmont and Brookline first so savings begin regardless.

rows.risk: Easton peak-week capacity is tighter than modelled
rows.mitigation: Pilot a peak week in December before committing; Fairmont takes overflow.
Exit penalty is already in the $2.6M; sublet is upside only.

slides.notes: The fourth beat. A risk without an owner reads as a problem.

slides.headline: Three approvals to start in November.

cards.title: Approve the plan
cards.body: Close Ridgeway, Brookline and Oakmont; Easton and Fairmont receive.

cards.title: $2.6M transition
cards.body: Released in three tranches, one per phase.

cards.title: Start union engagement
cards.body: Informal engagement at Ridgeway from Nov 1.

slides.band: Approve these three and the first saving lands in month four.
slides.notes: Small, concrete, sayable-yes-to in the room.
Backup: how the conclusion was reached, and detail for whoever asks.

slides.headline: Oakmont is the cheapest to exit and the first to go.
slides.source: Halvard depot P&L FY25; property schedule (fictional)
